__map.body:
# Kickoff: Pip and the Night (MTG-1)

chair: editor · invited: editor, writer-1, writer-2 · absent: none · room: story-room

## 1. The arc: what happens on each of the five pages (Pip afraid → meets night friends → not afraid) [G-3]
Round 1:
- writer-2: P1: Bedtime in the den. Pip pulls his tail over his eyes; outside, the dark is big and full of sounds. P2: A crackle! Pip peeks out, shaking. A glow blinks by: a firefly, lost from her friends. P3: Pip forgets to be scared and follows her into the dark to help. P4: The sounds turn out to be friends: an owl hooting hello, crickets singing, a hedgehog snuffling. P5: Firefly home, Pip curls up outside under the stars, listening. "Goodnight, night."
- writer-1: P1: Bedtime in the den. Shadows look huge; Pip pulls her tail over her eyes: The dark is too big. P2: A soft hoo-hoo. Pip peeks out the den door and meets Owl, who says wait and look; slowly the stars appear. P3: Fireflies blink a little path just outside the den, and Pip takes three brave steps. P4: The rustle is Hedgehog; the chirring is Cricket. Scary sounds now have names. P5: Back in bed, door open a crack, Pip says goodnight to each friend and sleeps.
- editor: Five pages, one beat each. P1: bedtime at the den mouth; the light goes, Pip (she) is afraid of the dark. P2: a sound in the dark; Pip takes a few brave steps out, no further than the big oak by the den. P3: the sound is a friend (Owl), who shows her more friends. P4: fireflies and the moon light the clearing; Pip sees the night is full of friends. P5: Pip back in the den, not afraid, says goodnight to the night. Refrain repeats on pages 1, 3 and 5. Pip never goes out of sight of the den; safety and home bookend the story.
**Decision:** Arc (binding for the bible and pages). Pip is a she/her fox throughout. P1: Bedtime in the den; shadows look huge, Pip pulls her tail over her eyes: the dark is too big. P2: A soft hoo-hoo; Pip peeks out the den door and meets Old Hoo the owl, who says wait and look; slowly the stars appear. P3: Glim and the fireflies blink a little path just outside the den; Pip takes three brave steps, no further than the big oak by the den door, always in sight of home. P4: The scary sounds get names: the rustle is Bristle the hedgehog (shy, a little scared of Pip too), the chirring is the cricket choir. P5: Back in bed, den door open a crack, Pip says goodnight to each friend and sleeps; last line "Goodnight, night." Pip does not go off into the dark alone and does not sleep outside. · actions: ISS-7

## 2. Tone and the night friends: who they are, how they sound [G-3]
Round 1:
- writer-2: Tone: warm, hushed, a whisper-to-read-aloud book; short sentences, gentle repetition ("Who is there?"), soft sound words a 4-year-old can join in on. Friends, each turning a scary sound into a kind one: Glim the firefly (small, brave, chirpy, speaks in quick bright bits), Old Hoo the owl (slow, deep, kind: "Hoo-hoo, hello"), the cricket choir (a chorus, "cree-cree"), Bristle the hedgehog (shy, snuffly, like Pip). No villain; the dark itself is never punished or explained away.
- writer-1: Tone: hushed and warm, read-aloud rhythm, short lines, one refrain per page: What is that in the night? No villain, no real danger, and nobody tells Pip her fear is silly; friends show, they do not lecture. Friends: Owl (slow, low, kind; Hoo is there? Only me), Fireflies (tiny, giggly, rhyming: blink, wink, follow the light), Cricket (rhythmic sound words: chirr-chirr, sing-song), Hedgehog (shy and snuffly, scared of Pip at first, which mirrors her).
- editor: Tone: warm, quiet, sleepy, read-aloud rhythm; short sentences, simple words for 4-6, nothing scary that is not resolved on the same page. Night friends: Owl (low, slow, kind "hoo"), the Fireflies (tiny, giggly, blinking), and Moon (soft, calm, watches over). Each friend has a signature sound children can join in on. Refrain: "The night is dark, but the night is kind."
**Decision:** Tone: hushed, warm, sleepy read-aloud; short lines, simple words for ages 4-6, soft sound words children can join in on. No villain, no real danger, nothing scary left unresolved on its page, and nobody tells Pip her fear is silly: friends show, they do not lecture. Refrain (one, on pages 1-4): "What is that in the night?" Page 5 closes on "Goodnight, night." Friends and names: Old Hoo the owl (slow, low, kind: "Hoo is there? Only me."), Glim the firefly with her fireflies (tiny, giggly, rhyming: "blink, wink, follow the light"), the cricket choir ("chirr-chirr", a sing-song chorus), Bristle the hedgehog (shy, snuffly, mirrors Pip). No Moon character; the stars simply appear.

## Whiteboard
### ideas
- Refrain on every page: "Who is there?" Pages 1-2 it is scared, pages 4-5 it is curious; the same words show the change. (writer-2)
- Keep Pip within sight of the den (and a grown-up fox) the whole time: ages 4-6 should not see wandering off alone at night modelled as brave. Bravery = peeking and a few steps, not a journey. (writer-1)

__map.title: Story bible
__map.accept: live/bench1-meta/work/BIBLE/page.md: a story bible for 'Pip and the Night' (ages 4-6) following the kickoff decisions (MTG-1 minutes in the lane:e channel). Sections: '## Characters' (each: name, one-line description; Pip is the hero; pronoun as decided), '## Setting', '## Page plan' with exactly five lines '- Page 1: …' to '- Page 5: …', one beat each, a complete arc (Pip afraid → meets night friends → not afraid). No words like scary, kill, die, dead, blood, hate, stupid.

__map.learned: Kickoff minutes fix she/her Pip, named friends (Old Hoo, Glim, Bristle, cricket choir), refrain on pages 1-4 and Pip never past the big oak; banned-word list forbids "scary" so the bible says "night sounds" instead.
Page 1 follows bible beat 1 only (shadows huge, tail over eyes, dark too big), ends on refrain; worry softened on-page (bed warm, den is home) per the bible rule.

Page 2: Old Hoo is she/her per bible ("she shows"); used exact line "Hoo is there? Only me."; stars appear on wait-and-look; no Moon. Ends with a curious glow leading into page 3 fireflies, then refrain.
Page 3: Glim (she) and fireflies light den-door-to-big-oak path; exactly three counted steps, Pip stops at the oak and looks back at home; ends with rustle/song lead-in to page 4, then refrain.
Bible matches MTG-1 decisions exactly (she/her Pip, named friends, oak boundary, refrain pages 1-4, no Moon); check pages against the oak/den-in-sight rule and refrain placement.
Page 1 hits beat 1 exactly (huge shadows, tail over eyes, dark too big), ~198 words, ends on refrain; no banned words or moon across all pages.
Page 2 follows beat 2 (hoo-hoo, peek at den door, Old Hoo line verbatim, wait and look, stars), ~214 words, Pip stays at den door, ends on refrain.
Page 3 follows beat 3: Glim (she) and fireflies light den-door-to-oak path, chant verbatim, exactly three steps, stops at the oak, den in sight; ~212 words; ends on refrain.

Page 4 follows beat 4: rustle named as Bristle (shy, afraid of Pip too, mirrored), chirring named as cricket choir (chirr-chirr), Pip stays at oak with den in sight, ends on refrain asked with a smile; ~205 words.

Page 5 follows beat 5: back in bed, door open a crack, goodnight to all four friends with their signature sounds verbatim, not afraid, falls asleep, last line "Goodnight, night."; ~182 words; no page-1-4 refrain; she/her, present tense; no banned words or moon.
Bible gives no pronoun for Bristle; avoided one. Refrain closes page 4 asked with a smile per beat.
Page 5 has no refrain per bible; each friend answers goodnight with its signature sound; ends exactly on "Goodnight, night."
